channel.title: ZeroTrace (EN)
channel.description: A daily cybersecurity newsletter: one concrete concept a day, for beginners and for those who want to go deeper.

item.title: Your TV gets security updates too (until one day it doesn't)
item.description: Why a smart TV needs patches just like your phone, how to let them install on their own, and what to do, without buying a new TV, when the manufacturer stops sending them.

item.title: Your home camera is only as secure as its app account
item.description: Why someone who wants to watch your cameras goes after your username and password, not the device, and the three app settings that stop them.

item.title: Having your files in the cloud isn't the same as having a backup
item.description: Why OneDrive, iCloud Drive, and Google Drive delete and encrypt right along with you, what safety net they really give you, and the copy you're missing. — Critical: Chrome: XML processing flaw already being exploited | Critical: Outlook: a crafted file hands over your password hash, already exploited

item.title: That bargain Android tablet may come with a stowaway installed at the factory
item.description: What an "uncertified" tablet is, why some arrive with a backdoor already on board, and the one-minute check to do before and after you buy.

item.title: That code to "vote" opens your WhatsApp to someone else
item.description: How the fake contest spreading on WhatsApp works, why the device-linking code is the key to your account, and one simple rule so you never fall for it. — Heads-up: OpenSSH on Alpine Linux: a very long password lets attackers log in without the real one

item.title: Your photos know where you took them
item.description: What data rides along hidden inside a photo, when it can give away where you live, and how to share pictures without handing out your home address. — Heads-up: Apple: a 2024 WebKit flaw now under attack on unpatched devices

item.title: If someone steals your phone after watching you type the passcode
item.description: Why your unlock passcode opens far more than the screen, what the theft protections on iPhone and Android actually do, and what to have ready before it happens. — Critical: SonicWall: SSL VPN flaw that bypasses SAML, now exploited | Heads-up: Zyxel GS1900 switches: exploited flaw that slipped past the earlier patch

item.title: Your Windows 10 PC: make sure it's still getting patches
item.description: Microsoft will keep shipping security fixes through October 12, 2027—but only to enrolled PCs. And many desktops that "can't run" Windows 11 just have one setting turned off. — Heads-up: Chrome 157 fixes 213 flaws, seven of them critical

item.title: Don't ignore your browser's certificate warning
item.description: What “Your connection is not private” means, how an attacker could exploit it, and what to check before you continue. — Heads-up: Firefox 159.0.1 fixes a high-impact security flaw

item.title: Your laptop is already encrypted. Do you know where the key is?
item.description: Windows and macOS encrypt your drive with barely a prompt. That protects you if it's stolen, but if it ever asks for the recovery key and you don't have it, your files are gone. — Critical: WordPress: update-process flaw now under attack

item.title: Your TV knows what you're watching
item.description: What automatic content recognition is, why it works even with your console or laptop plugged in over HDMI, and how to turn it off in five minutes. — Critical: Ivanti Connect Secure: corporate VPN hit by chained flaws | Critical: PHP2Shell: two critical PHP flaws added to the exploited list | Heads-up: Android: November patch fixes a critical zero-click flaw
